	ch := make(chan int, 1)

If several select cases are ready, which one runs?
options: A pseudorandom ready one, not necessarily the first in source
Always the topmost in the source

questions.text: Why is close often used as a “no more work” signal?
options: close copies every value into main
All waiting receives wake and see the close; range ends

questions.text: How does receive from nil differ from receive from a closed empty channel?
options: Both yield ok false at once
nil blocks; closed yields zero and ok false at once
nil yields ok false; closed blocks

questions.text: Can you reopen a closed channel?
options: Yes, another make on the same variable — that is a different channel
No: that channel stays closed; only a new make is a new channel

questions.text: Why is send-only useful in a sender’s API?
options: The compiler will not let it receive and accidentally drain the channel
Then the channel cannot be nil

questions.text: What is wrong with “guessing” the order of two ready cases without default?
options: The order is always source order
The choice among ready cases is not deterministic — a one-log code question would race

questions.text: What does close(nil) do?
Can one goroutine both send and receive on one unbuffered channel with no other side?
options: No: unbuffered send waits for another goroutine — deadlock

questions.text: Buffer as a sliding window between producer and consumer: cap is what?
options: How many values can sit without send/recv meeting at the same moment

questions.text: Why is a signal channel often chan struct{}?
options: The empty value carries nothing; the send/close is the signal

questions.text: After close, another receive (empty buffer) — does it block?
options: No: immediate zero and ok false, no matter how many times

questions.text: Is channel direction a property of the value or of the variable?
options: Only a runtime flag inside the channel
It lives on the heap next to the buffer
It is the variable/parameter type: the same channel can be seen as chan, chan<-, or <-chan

questions.text: Can you close through a send-only (chan<-) variable?
options: No, close takes only bidirectional chan T
Yes, close(chan<- T) compiles; you cannot close a <-chan T
Yes, but only after cap sends

questions.text: Select fairness: does the runtime round-robin each case on a quantum?
options: Only a random choice among the ready; not round-robin for sleeping cases
Always default if present, else round-robin
By hash of the channel pointer

questions.text: Why set `ch = nil` after handling a case in a select loop?
options: So that branch is never chosen again

questions.text: Does passing a channel by value copy the buffer?
options: Only the pointer is copied; there is one buffer

questions.text: Can close wake several waiting receives?
options: Yes, every receive waiting on that channel sees the close

questions.text: Send on closed and close(nil) — what do they share?
Why can’t you “guess” output if two goroutines both send into a buffer of 2 with no wait order?
options: Send order is not fixed — a question needs happens-before
Print from a channel always sorts

questions.text: Does an empty struct{} in a channel occupy a buffer slot?
options: No, cap is ignored for struct{}
No, such sends do not count
Yes, each send takes one len slot even if the value is empty

questions.text: If several select cases are ready, one of them is chosen pseudorandomly.
A closed channel can be opened with the same close.
Receive from nil blocks; from a closed empty channel it does not.
close(nil) is safe.
The same channel can be passed as chan<- and as <-chan.
Unbuffered send and receive in one goroutine without select are always safe.
close wakes everyone waiting to receive on that channel.
Passing a channel copies the whole buffer.
After closing an empty channel, receive never blocks again.
select always takes the first ready case from the top of the file.
Assigning ch = nil disables the case that uses that ch in select.
close on chan<- T compiles; on <-chan T it does not.
chan struct{} is handy when the event matters, not a payload.
cap depends on whether the channel is closed.
Another receive from a closed empty channel again yields zero and ok false.
Two ready sends in select without default give a stable log order.
len counts occupied buffer slots, even for struct{}.
Send on a closed channel is ok false, not a panic.
A new make on the same variable is a different channel.
Nil and a closed channel behave the same on receive.
How does select choose among several ready cases?
questions.answer: Pseudorandomly one of the ready ones.

questions.text: close as a signal — what is the idea?
questions.answer: All waiting receives see the end of the stream; range returns.

questions.text: nil vs closed empty on receive?
questions.answer: nil blocks; closed is immediate zero and ok false.

questions.text: What does close(nil) do?
questions.answer: It panics.

questions.text: Can you reopen a closed channel?
questions.answer: No. Only a new make is a new channel.

questions.text: Where does direction live?
questions.answer: In the variable’s type, not inside the buffer.

questions.text: Why ch = nil in a select loop?
questions.answer: To disable that branch.

questions.text: Is the buffer copied when assigning a channel?
questions.answer: No, a reference to the same channel is copied.

questions.text: close and several waiting receives?
questions.answer: They all wake.

questions.text: Unbuffered send and recv in one goroutine?
questions.answer: Deadlock: nobody to meet.

questions.text: Why chan struct{} for a signal?
questions.answer: No payload; the event/close is what matters.

questions.text: Is the order of two ready cases stable?
questions.answer: No.

questions.text: Receive after close of empty — a block?
questions.answer: No, always zero and ok false.

questions.text: close(chan<- T)?
questions.answer: It compiles. You cannot close a <-chan T.

questions.text: Send on closed?
questions.answer: Panic.

questions.text: What does a new make on the same variable give?
questions.answer: A different channel; the old one is not “reopened”.

questions.text: len for struct{} in the buffer?
questions.answer: Each send occupies a slot.

questions.text: Does select guarantee round-robin for sleeping cases?
questions.answer: No, only a random choice among those already ready.

questions.text: How to disable a case without deleting code?
questions.answer: Store nil in that variable.

questions.text: One channel, two views?
questions.answer: Yes: chan T, chan<- T, <-chan T — one object.
